title: CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life
chineseTitle: 第 17 章：对生活的新兴趣

paragraphs.en: Anne was sewing in the kitchen when she noticed Diana beckoning from the Dryad’s Bubble beckon. She rushed outside, her eyes reflecting both hope and astonishment.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮正在厨房里缝纫，忽然看到戴安娜从“林德女士的泡泡”那边招手。她赶紧跑出去，眼中同时流露出希望与惊讶的神情。

paragraphs.en: Diana's face was downcast. "Your mother hasn't changed her mind?" Anne asked, her voice trembling.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜的脸沉了下来。“你妈妈还没改变主意？”安妮的声音微微颤抖着问道。

paragraphs.en: "No," Diana replied sadly. "She says I can never play with you again. I've been crying, telling her it wasn’t your fault, but to no avail."
paragraphs.zh: “不，”戴安娜悲伤地回答，“她说我永远不能再和你一起玩了。我已经哭着告诉她这并不是你的错，但毫无用处。”

paragraphs.en: Anne’s eyes filled with tears. "Ten minutes isn't long enough for a farewell." She clasped her hands together.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的眼中盈满了泪水。“十分钟时间未免太短，不足以道别。”她紧紧地握住了双手。

paragraphs.en: "Diana, will you promise to never forget me?"
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜，你能不能答应我永远不要忘了我？

paragraphs.en: "I'll keep my promise," Diana sobbed. "I can't have another bosom friend—I don’t want one. I love you more than anyone."
paragraphs.zh: “我一定遵守诺言，”戴安娜抽泣道，“我不需要另一个知心朋友——我也不会想要。我会比任何人都更加爱你。”

paragraphs.en: Anne’s voice quivered as she asked, “Do you love me?”
paragraphs.zh: 安妮的声音微微颤抖着问道：“你爱我吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, of course,” Diana replied. “Didn’t you know that?”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，我知道。”戴安娜回答道，“你不知道吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” Anne admitted. “I never hoped for such a deep affection.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”安妮承认道，“我从没想过会有如此深厚的情感。”

paragraphs.en: Diana promised to always love Anne, and Anne solemnly offered her a lock of hair.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜承诺永远爱着安妮，安妮庄重地向她许下一根头发的誓言。

paragraphs.en: “Have you something to cut it with?” Diana asked, wiping away tears.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜一边擦着眼泪，问道：“你有没有什么东西可以把它割开？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, my patchwork scissors are in my pocket,” Anne said. She carefully clipped one curl from Diana’s hair.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我的拼补剪刀在口袋里，”安妮说。她仔细地从戴安娜的头发上剪下了一缕卷发。

paragraphs.en: Farewell, dear friend, she thought. Though we live side by side, we must now be strangers. But your memory will always shine like a star over my life.
paragraphs.zh: 再见了，亲爱的朋友，她心想。虽然我们住在同一片屋檐下，现在我们必须成为陌路人。但你在我生命中的记忆将永远像星辰般璀璨。

paragraphs.en: Anne watched Diana leave, waving her hand sadly until she was out of sight. She returned home, somewhat comforted by their romantic farewell.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮目送戴安娜离去，悲伤地挥手直到她的身影消失不见。她回到家时，心中多少得到了一些安慰，因为这次充满浪漫意味的告别让她感到温暖。

paragraphs.en: "Everything is finished," Anne told Marilla. "I won't have another friend like Diana. Even with Katie and Violetta gone, it's worse now.
paragraphs.zh: “一切都结束了，”安妮对玛丽拉说，“我不再会有像戴安娜那样的朋友了。即使凯蒂和维奥莱塔不在了，现在的情况更糟糕。”

paragraphs.en: Diana and I had a touching goodbye by the spring. We used 'thou' and 'thee,' which felt more romantic than just 'you.' She gave me a lock of her hair, which I'll keep forever.
paragraphs.zh: 在春日里，戴安娜和我依依惜别。我们使用“汝”和“尔”，感觉比仅仅用“你”要浪漫得多。她送给我一根她的头发，我会永远珍藏。

paragraphs.en: "I'm going back to school," Anne declared on Monday morning, surprising Marilla with her determination. "It's all I have left now that Diana is gone."
paragraphs.zh: “我要回学校了，”安妮星期一早上宣布，她的决心让玛丽拉感到惊讶。“现在戴安娜走了，这是我唯一的选择了。”

paragraphs.en: "Focus on your studies," Marilla advised. "I hope you won't cause any trouble this time."
paragraphs.zh: “专心学习吧，”玛丽拉建议道，“我希望这次你不会再惹出什么麻烦。”

paragraphs.en: Anne agreed dejectedly. She felt the routine might be easier now. Mr. Phillips said Minnie Andrews was a model pupil, but she lacked imagination and seemed dull.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮沮丧地应允了。她觉得现在这种例行公事或许会轻松一些。菲利普斯先生说米妮·安德鲁斯是个模范学生，但她缺乏想象力，显得有些乏味。

paragraphs.en: "I'll try to be good," Anne said. "But I doubt there will be much fun in it. I can't bear going by the Birch Path alone; I'd cry if I did."
paragraphs.zh: “我会试着做个好女孩，”安妮说，“但恐怕乐趣不会太多。我一个人走橡树小径实在受不了；那样我会哭的。”

paragraphs.en: Anne returned to school and quickly regained her place. Her classmates welcomed her back warmly, missing her imagination in games, voice in singing, and dramatic flair during book readings at dinner. Ruby Gillis secretly passed three blue plums to her during a test reading session.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮回到学校，很快又找到了自己的位置。同学们热烈欢迎她的归来，怀念她在游戏中的想象力、唱歌时的声音以及晚餐读书时的戏剧性表现。在一次测读会话中，鲁比·吉尔斯悄悄递给她三颗蓝李子。

paragraphs.en: Ella May MacPherson presented Anne with an elaborate yellow pansy cut from a floral catalogue, a prized decoration in Avonlea school.
paragraphs.zh: 埃拉·梅·麦克弗森送给安妮一束精美的黄色三色堇，这是从埃文利学校花名录上剪下来的，被视为学校的珍贵装饰。

paragraphs.en: Sophia Sloane offered to teach Anne a new pattern of knit lace, perfect for apron trimming. Katie Boulter gave Anne a perfume bottle for slate water, and Julia Bell wrote a poem on scalloped pink paper:
paragraphs.zh: 索菲亚·斯ло恩主动教安妮编织蕾丝的新花样，这种蕾丝非常适合用来装饰围裙。凯蒂·博尔特送给安妮一瓶用于石板水的香水，而朱莉娅·贝尓则在波纹粉红色纸上为她写了一首诗。

paragraphs.en: "When twilight drops her curtain down And pins it with a star Remember that you have a friend Though she may wander far."
paragraphs.zh: 当黄昏拉下帷幕，用星辰钉牢 备忘你有一位朋友，即便她远行千里。

paragraphs.en: Anne felt appreciated when Marilla heard her sighing happily. However, not all appreciation came from the girls. After dinner, Mr. Phillips instructed Anne to sit with model Minnie Andrews.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮感到很受赏识，因为玛丽拉听到了她快乐地叹了口气。不过，并非所有的赞赏都来自女孩们。晚饭后，菲利普斯先生让安妮坐在模特米妮·安德鲁斯旁边。

paragraphs.en: On her desk was a large, luscious "strawberry apple." Anne hesitated, remembering that strawberry apples only grew in the Blythe orchard across Lake of Shining Waters. She dropped the apple and wiped her fingers on her handkerchief.
paragraphs.zh: 她的桌上放着一个大而鲜美的“草莓苹果”。安妮犹豫了一下，想起这种水果只生长在湖光水色湖对面布里思果园中。她放下苹果，用手帕擦了擦手指。

paragraphs.en: The apple remained untouched until Timothy Andrews swept it away as his perquisite.
paragraphs.zh: 这颗苹果一直未动，直到蒂莫西·安德鲁斯把它顺手牵走。

paragraphs.en: Charlie Sloane's pencil, adorned with striped red and yellow paper costing two cents, was more warmly received by Anne. She accepted it graciously and rewarded Charlie with a smile that sent him into raptures, causing him to make errors in dictation during class.
paragraphs.zh: 查理·斯洛恩的铅笔上缠着两毛钱买的条纹红黄纸，这让安妮感到格外高兴。她欣然接受了这支铅笔，并冲他一笑，看得查理心花怒放，在课堂上竟然出现了打字错误。

paragraphs.en: Yet, Diana Barry’s absence of any tribute or recognition, sitting with Gertie Pye, made Anne's triumph taste bitter.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，戴安娜·巴里的缺席让安妮与吉蒂·派伊坐在一起的胜利变得苦涩。

paragraphs.en: That night, Diana confided to Marilla that she might have smiled at Anne once. The next morning, a note and a small parcel were handed to Anne by Diana.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，戴安娜向玛丽拉透露，她曾经对安妮微微一笑。第二天一早，戴安娜交给安妮一张便条和一个小包裹。

paragraphs.en: Diana's note read: "Dear Anne, Mother says I can't play or talk with you even in school. It isn't my fault; don't be cross. I miss you terribly and love you as much as ever.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜的信写道：“亲爱的安妮，妈妈说即便在学校里也不能和你一起玩或说话。这并不是我的错，别生我的气。我非常想念你，依然像从前一样爱你。”

paragraphs.en: I made you a new bookmark out of red tissue paper—only three girls know how to make them now. Remember this when you look at it. Your true friend, Diana Barry."
paragraphs.zh: 我用红色薄绸纸给你做了一个新的书签——现在会这个手艺的只剩下三个女孩了。看到它的时候，别忘了这是戴安娜·巴里真正的朋友送给你的。“

paragraphs.en: Anne replied promptly: "My own darling Diana: Of course I'm not cross because you have to obey your mother. Our spirits can still communicate. I'll keep your lovely present forever.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮迅速回答道：“我最亲爱的戴安娜：当然，我知道你必须听你妈妈的话。我们的精神依然可以相通。我会永远珍藏你送给我的这份可爱礼物。”

paragraphs.en: Minnie Andrews is nice but has no imagination—after being Diana's best friend, I can't be her. Please excuse my poor spelling; it's much improved now. Yours until death us do part, Anne or Cordelia Shirley."
paragraphs.zh: 米妮·安德鲁斯不错，但缺乏想象力——自从我和戴安娜成为最好的朋友后，我就不能再和她那样了。请原谅我糟糕的拼写；我现在进步多了。直到生死相隔，安妮或科黛拉·谢里登才会如此与你相伴。

paragraphs.en: P.S.: Tonight, I'll sleep with your letter under my pillow. A. OR C.S.
paragraphs.zh: 附言：今晚，我會把你的信放在枕下。是A，還是C.S.?

paragraphs.en: Anne surprised everyone by excelling in her studies after returning to school. She focused intensely on her lessons, determined not to be outdone by Gilbert Blythe. Their rivalry became evident; while Gilbert's was friendly, Anne’s was fueled by a persistent grudge.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮回到学校后竟然在学业上取得了优异的成绩，这让 everyone 都感到意外。她全身心地投入到学习中，决心不让吉尔伯特·布雷思;'; 脱口而出'超越自己。两人之间的竞争变得明显起来；吉尔伯特的竞争还带有一丝友好的意味，而安妮的则被一种持续的怨恨所驱动。

paragraphs.en: They alternated as top students—Anne often besting Gilbert with her red braids flying. One day they tied for first place, causing both embarrassment and satisfaction.
paragraphs.zh: 他们在成绩上交替领先——安妮常常凭借她飘扬的红发战胜吉尔伯特。有一天，两人并列第一，既让他们感到尴尬又颇为得意。

paragraphs.en: Gilbert maintained his head of the spelling class one month, but the next Anne outperformed him in arithmetic after a night of studying decimals. Their competition was intense during monthly written exams; Gilbert led by three marks initially, then Anne beat him by five. However, Gilbert's congratulations before the whole school dampened her joy.
paragraphs.zh: 吉尔伯特在拼写课上保持了第一名一个月，但安妮在研究小数后的算术考试中后来居上。每月一次的笔试竞争异常激烈；起初，吉尔伯特领先三分，随后安妮反超了五分。然而，在全校师生面前向吉尔伯特表示祝贺却让她的喜悦大打折扣。

paragraphs.en: Despite Mr. Phillips’s teaching methods, Anne made significant progress due to her determination. By term’s end, both she and Gilbert were promoted to the fifth class, studying Latin, geometry, French, and algebra. Geometry proved particularly challenging for Anne.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管菲利普斯先生的教学方法不尽人意，安妮凭借自己的决心取得了显著的进步。学期结束时，她和吉尔伯特都被提升到了五年级，学习拉丁文、几何、法语和代数。对于安妮来说，几何尤其具有挑战性。

paragraphs.en: She found it dull and unimaginative, even though Mr. Phillips deemed her the worst student at it. Her frustration was palpable as she confided in Marilla about her struggles.
paragraphs.zh: 她觉得这门课既枯燥又缺乏想象力，尽管菲利普斯先生认为她是班上最差的学生。她的沮丧之情溢于言表，向玛丽拉倾诉了自己的困扰。

paragraphs.en: Diana and I get along better than before. Though we now meet as strangers, my love for Diana remains unquenchable. It saddens me at times to think about her.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜和我相处得比以前更好了。尽管我们现在像陌生人一样见面，我对戴安娜的爱依旧未曾消减。有时想到她，还是会让我感到一丝伤感。

paragraphs.en: Yet, Marilla, this fascinating world prevents us from staying sad for long.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，玛丽拉，这个迷人的世界让我们很难长久地沉浸在悲伤中。
